intro.title: Remove K Digits
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a function that removes k digits from a given number string to produce the smallest possible resulting number. You will learn the core concept of using a monotonic stack to efficiently process the digits while maintaining the smallest sequence. The main technologies involved are JavaScript strings, arrays, and stack operations. This beginner-friendly lesson will guide you step-by-step through the logic and implementation, helping you understand how to solve this classic algorithmic problem.
intro.usecase: The 'Remove K Digits' algorithm solves optimization problems where you need to minimize numerical values by selectively removing characters while preserving order. This pattern appears in financial applications where transaction IDs or account numbers must be shortened while maintaining their sequence integrity. For example, banking dashboards might display truncated account numbers that remain valid identifiers, and data visualization tools could compress long numeric labels on charts without altering their comparative relationships. Developers implement this when designing systems that need to present the smallest possible valid representation of sequential numeric data.
